title: Airflow and Cooling
summary: Use airflow and temperature clues to understand why cooling supports reliable computing.
objectives: Identify a possible airflow problem from a safe diagram or description.

vocab.def: The place where air enters a system.
The place where used or warmer air leaves a system.

sections.heading: Computing produces heat
sections.body: Servers use energy while they work, and some of that energy becomes heat. Too much heat can make equipment unreliable, so facilities plan how air moves around equipment.

sections.heading: Read the airflow
sections.body: Cooler air enters through an intake, moves around equipment, and warmer air leaves through an exhaust. Blocked paths or mixed airflow can make cooling less effective.

sections.heading: Study diagrams safely
sections.body: Use arrows on a paper rack diagram to identify intake, exhaust, and a blocked path. Do not service HVAC equipment or open energized hardware. Those tasks require qualified supervision.

practice.prompt: A diagram shows warm exhaust air being pulled back into a server intake. What evidence suggests an airflow problem, and what safe next step would you recommend?

quiz.question: Why does airflow matter around servers?
options: It helps move heat away from equipment
quiz.answer: It helps move heat away from equipment

reflectionPrompt: What clue would make you investigate cooling instead of networking?
